explain: After a help verb like kan, the next verb is in the infinitive: kan prata.

fun.sv: Jag kan prata svenska. Bara inte när någon lyssnar.
fun.en: I can speak Swedish. Just not when someone is listening.

explain: With no help verb, the verb is in the present tense with -r: hon pratar.

fun.sv: Hon pratar svenska varje dag. Med katten.
fun.en: She speaks Swedish every day. With the cat.

explain: After the help verb vill, use the infinitive: vill dricka.

fun.sv: Katten vill inte dricka från skålen. Han vill dricka från kranen.
fun.en: The cat doesn’t want to drink from his bowl. He wants to drink from the tap.

hint: He drinks tea in the morning.
explain: With no help verb, use the present tense: han dricker.

fun.sv: Mormor dricker kaffe klockan nio på kvällen och sover som en baby.
fun.en: Grandma drinks coffee at nine in the evening and sleeps like a baby.

explain: Bo is a Group III verb: it just adds -r, so jag bor.

fun.sv: Jag bor i en liten lägenhet. Katten bor i hela lägenheten.
fun.en: I live in a small flat. The cat lives in the whole flat.

prompt: De ska ___ till Stockholm i maj.
hint: They’re going to travel to Stockholm in May.
explain: After the help verb ska, use the infinitive: ska resa.

fun.sv: I februari ska alla finländare resa till Spanien. Samtidigt.
fun.en: In February all Finns are going to travel to Spain. At the same time.

hint: I usually cook in the evening.
explain: Brukar is a help verb, so the next verb is in the infinitive: brukar laga.

fun.sv: Jag brukar laga mat på kvällen. Brandlarmet brukar hjälpa till.
fun.en: I usually cook in the evening. The smoke alarm usually helps.

explain: After the help verb måste, use the infinitive: måste jobba.

fun.sv: Du måste jobba imorgon, men ingen säger att du måste vara vaken.
fun.en: You have to work tomorrow, but nobody says you have to be awake.

explain: Stänga is a Group II verb, so the command form drops the -a: Stäng!

fun.sv: Stäng dörren! Myggorna vill också komma in.
fun.en: Close the door! The mosquitoes want to come in too.

explain: Lyssna is a Group I verb, so the command form is the same as the infinitive: Lyssna!

fun.sv: – Lyssna på mig! sa jag till katten. Katten gick.
fun.en: “Listen to me!” I said to the cat. The cat left.

explain: Skriva is a Group IV verb, so the command form drops the -a: Skriv!

fun.sv: Skriv ditt namn här. Nej, inte på bordet!
fun.en: Write your name here. No, not on the table!

hint: You don’t need to book a table at McDonald’s.
explain: “Don’t need to” is behöver inte; Swedish doesn’t use måste inte, and får inte means “not allowed”.

fun.sv: Du behöver inte ställa klockan. Katten väcker dig klockan fem.
fun.en: You don’t need to set the alarm. The cat wakes you at five.

prompt: Vi ___ ta med mat, det finns lunch.
hint: We don’t need to bring food; there is lunch.
explain: Something that isn’t necessary takes behöver inte, never måste inte.

fun.sv: Vi behöver inte ta med mat. Mormor har lagat mat för tjugo personer.
fun.en: We don’t need to bring food. Grandma has cooked for twenty people.

hint: You’re not allowed to smoke here.
explain: Får inte means “not allowed, must not”.

fun.sv: Fåren får inte komma in i köket.
fun.en: The sheep aren’t allowed into the kitchen.
fun.note: Pun: får means both ‘sheep’ and ‘may, is allowed to’.

explain: Får means “may, be allowed to”, so Får jag …? asks for permission.

fun.sv: Får jag låna din penna? Jag ger tillbaka den. Kanske.
fun.en: May I borrow your pen? I’ll give it back. Maybe.

explain: Borde means “ought to, should”.

fun.sv: Jag borde sova. Men katten tycker att det är fest.
fun.en: I ought to sleep. But the cat thinks it’s party time.

explain: Brukar means “usually”: jag brukar cykla = I usually cycle.

fun.sv: Jag brukar cykla till jobbet. Från maj till juni.
fun.en: I usually cycle to work. From May to June.

hint: She wants to become a doctor.
explain: Vill means “want to”.

fun.sv: Min dotter vill bli läkare. Min son vill bli katt.
fun.en: My daughter wants to become a doctor. My son wants to become a cat.

prompt: Jag är sjuk, jag ___ stanna hemma.
hint: I’m ill, I have to stay at home.
explain: Måste means “must, have to”.

fun.sv: Jag måste stanna hemma idag. Soffan behöver mig.
fun.en: I have to stay at home today. The sofa needs me.

explain: Kunde is the past form of kan: couldn’t = kunde inte.

fun.sv: Jag kunde inte komma igår. Katten satt på mina nycklar.
fun.en: I couldn’t come yesterday. The cat was sitting on my keys.

hint: The children didn’t want to sleep.
explain: Ville is the past form of vill: didn’t want to = ville inte.

fun.sv: Barnen ville inte sova. Nu sover alla utom barnen.
fun.en: The children didn’t want to sleep. Now everyone is asleep except the children.

prompt: Jag ___ vilja ha en kopp kaffe.
hint: I would like a cup of coffee.
explain: Skulle vilja is the polite way to say “would like”.

fun.sv: Jag skulle vilja ha en kopp kaffe. Eller en hink.
fun.en: I would like a cup of coffee. Or a bucket.

hint: She reads a book every week.
ask: Write the verb in the present tense.
explain: Läsa is a Group II verb: the -a becomes -er, so hon läser.

fun.sv: Hon läser en bok varje vecka. Det är samma bok.
fun.en: She reads a book every week. It’s the same book.

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb kan, the verb stays in the infinitive: kan du köra.

fun.sv: – Kan du köra bil? – Ja, men bara framåt.
fun.en: “Can you drive a car?” “Yes, but only forwards.”

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb måste, use the infinitive: måste gå.

fun.sv: Jag måste gå nu. Det har jag sagt i en timme.
fun.en: I have to go now. I’ve been saying that for an hour.

prompt: Vi ska ___ ett mejl till läraren. (skriva)
hint: We are going to write an email to the teacher.
ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb ska, use the infinitive: ska skriva.

fun.sv: Vi ska skriva till läraren: ”Hunden åt läxan.” Men vi har ingen hund.
fun.en: We’re going to write to the teacher: “The dog ate the homework.” But we have no dog.

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb vill, use the infinitive: vill dricka.

fun.sv: Hon vill dricka te. Katten vill dricka hennes te.
fun.en: She wants to drink tea. The cat wants to drink her tea.

hint: The children usually sleep late on Saturdays.
ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After the help verb brukar, use the infinitive: brukar sova.

fun.sv: Barnen brukar sova länge på skoldagar. På lördagar vaknar de klockan sex.
fun.en: The children usually sleep late on school days. On Saturdays they wake up at six.

ask: Write the right form of the verb.
explain: After borde, use the infinitive: borde börja.

fun.sv: Jag borde börja träna. Jag har redan köpt skorna.
fun.en: I ought to start exercising. I’ve already bought the shoes.

explain: Vet is for facts and information: jag vet svaret.

fun.sv: Jag vet svaret! Vad var frågan?
fun.en: I know the answer! What was the question?

prompt: Jag ___ Anna. Hon är min granne.
hint: I know Anna. She’s my neighbour.
explain: Känner is for people: jag känner Anna.

fun.sv: Jag känner min granne. Vi har sagt hej två gånger på fem år.
fun.en: I know my neighbour. We’ve said hi twice in five years.

hint: Do you know where the station is?
explain: Where the station is = information, so vet.

fun.sv: – Vet du var stationen är? – Ja. Tack för frågan.
fun.en: “Do you know where the station is?” “Yes. Thanks for asking.”

explain: Peter is a person, so känner.

fun.sv: – Känner du Peter? – Nej, men min katt känner honom. Peter har fisk.
fun.en: “Do you know Peter?” “No, but my cat knows him. Peter has fish.”
